Status of flora in Nepal and world representation
Fungi: General introduction and characteristic features of phycomycetes, ascomycetes, basidiomycetes and deuteromycetes
Structure and reproduction of Mucor and Yeast
Introduction of Mushrooms, poisonous and non-poisonous mushrooms, economic importance of fungi

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Classification organises millions of species into a hierarchy (KPCOFGS) whose basic unit is the species. Linnaeus gave biology its naming system — binomial nomenclature (Genus + specific epithet, italicised, e.g. *Mangifera indica*) — and its first two-kingdom scheme.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: Parent-chain + locant(s) + sub-prefix + suffix = IUPAC name

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Domain vs kingdom:** domains are a newer, higher rank above kingdoms; the five kingdoms are still taught, but Monera is split into Bacteria and Archaea at the domain level.  ·  **Fungi are not plants:** chitin (not cellulose) walls, absorptive (not photosynthetic) nutrition, glycogen (not starch) reserve — Whittaker's main correction to the two-kingdom system.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Binomial nomenclature is a guaranteed 2-mark item somewhere in the paper — capitalisation, italics and the author abbreviation are what examiners check.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Mangifera indica*** — mango; Plantae; the standard binomial example (Linn.).  ·  ***Homo sapiens*** — human; Animalia; binomial with lowercase epithet.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Nutrition as the kingdom separator** — photosynthesis → Plantae; absorption → Fungi; ingestion → Animalia; mixed → Protista.  ·  **Molecular data outrank appearance** — Archaea look bacterial but rRNA proves a separate domain.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Classification = arranging organisms into taxa by similarities and evolutionary relationships; purposes: identification, organisation, relationship, prediction, universal naming.  ·  Basis evolved: morphology (Linnaeus) → cell structure/nutrition (Whittaker) → rRNA genes (Woese).  ·  Hierarchy: Kingdom → Division/Phylum → Class → Order → Family → Genus → Species ("KPCOFGS"); species = basic unit.  ·  Binomial nomenclature — Linnaeus, *Species Plantarum* 1753: Genus (capital) + specific epithet (lower), italicised/underlined, Latin, unique, with author abbreviation.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Linnaeus = Father of Taxonomy; *Species Plantarum* (1753) is the starting point of botanical nomenclature.  ·  About 1.8 million species described; estimates of total species run to 8–9 million.

rows.label: More practice
rows.text: **Short answer (2m):** On what three criteria is the five-kingdom system based? **Answer.** 1. **Cell structure** — prokaryotic or eukaryotic. 2. **Level of body organisation** — unicellular, colonial or multicellular. 3. **Mode of nutrition** — photosynthetic (autotrophic), absorptive or ingestive.  ·  **Short answer (2m):** Why were fungi removed from Plantae? **Answer.** Three plant-unlike features: 1. cell walls of **chitin**, not cellulose; 2. **absorptive heterotrophy** — they digest food externally and absorb it, instead of photosynthesising; 3. reserve food is **glycogen**, not starch.  ·  **Long answer (5m):** Describe the five-kingdom classification with merits and demerits. **Answer.** **Proposed by R. H. Whittaker (1969)** on three criteria — cell structure, body organisation and mode of nutrition.…

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: ***Euglena*** — Protista; boundary organism: chloroplasts AND ingestion — shows why Protista is a mixed kingdom.  ·  ***Methanococcus*** — Archaea; produces methane in anaerobic habitats (cow rumen, marshes).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Why Classification Is the First Question of Biology Biology names and organises life before it explains it. With an estimated 8–9 million species on Earth (about 1.8 million described so far), no science is possible without a **system of naming** and a **system of grouping**.…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Conceptual Understanding — What Classification Is ### 2.1 Definition and purpose **Classification (taxonomy)** is the arrangement of organisms into groups (taxa) on the basis of their similarities, differences and evolutionary relationships.…  ·  ## 3. Binomial Nomenclature — The Naming System ### 3.1 What it is **Binomial nomenclature** is the two-word scientific naming system in which every organism receives a name of **Genus + specific epithet**, e.g. *Mangifera indica* (mango), *Homo sapiens* (human).…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Three domains (Woese 1990, rRNA-based): Bacteria (peptidoglycan), Archaea (no peptidoglycan, extremophiles), Eukarya (true nucleus).  ·  Five kingdoms (Whittaker 1969) on cell structure + organisation + nutrition: Monera (prokaryote), Protista (unicellular eukaryote), Fungi (absorptive, chitin), Plantae (photosynthetic), Animalia (ingestive).  ·  Merits: separated prokaryotes, removed fungi from plants, phylogenetic direction; demerits: Protista/Monera are mixed groups, boundary organisms (Euglena, viruses) awkward.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Cyanobacteria are Monera, not algae:** "blue-green algae" is a historical name; they are prokaryotic photosynthesizers, so they belong to Bacteria, not Protista or Plantae.  ·  **Species epithet alone is not a name:** "indica" names nothing by itself; only the full binomial (*Mangifera indica*) identifies a species.  ·  **Protista vs Monera:** both mostly unicellular, but Protista are eukaryotic (true nucleus, organelles) while Monera are prokaryotic.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: "Classify the five kingdoms" appeared in BOTH 2022 and 2024 papers (5 marks each) — this is the highest-frequency long question of the unit; practise the full award structure.  ·  "Classification is a hypothesis of evolutionary relationship, not a filing cabinet."  ·  "Genes, not appearance, draw the deepest lines in life's tree."

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: "Fungi: chitin + absorption" — the two-word answer that separates fungi from plants.  ·  **Long answer (5m):** Explain the three-domain system and its relationship to the five-kingdom system. **Answer.** **Proposed by Carl Woese (1990)** from **16S/18S rRNA gene sequences** — the most conserved molecules in life, so they record deep ancestry.…  ·  **Conceptual (3m):** Why is the species called the basic unit of classification? **Answer.** Because it is the **only rank that corresponds to a real biological entity**: a naturally interbreeding, reproductively isolated population sharing one gene pool.…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Conceptual (3m):** Why do scientific names remain stable while common names do not? **Answer.** Binomials are governed by **international codes** (ICBN/ICZN) with fixed rules — Latin (language-neutral), **unique worldwide**, published with a description and tied to a **type specimen**, and changed only by formal…  ·  **Application (2m):** A farmer reports a new crop disease organism that has no nucleus and no peptidoglycan but lives in a hot spring. Predict its domain and one property. **Answer.** **Domain: Archaea** — prokaryotic (no nucleus) but lacking peptidoglycan rules out Bacteria, and a hot-spring habitat fits the archaeal…  ·  Why did Whittaker need three criteria while Linnaeus needed only one? **Answer.** Linnaeus classified a world that knew only plants and animals, and a single visible criterion — **overall form** — was enough to sort them.…
